Copilot commented on this pull request.

Pull request overview

Integrates real OpenAI Chat Completions (gpt-4o) into the FastAPI backend and upgrades the frontend from alert()-based mode switching to an in-page chat UI so users can interact with NOVA/DRAGON modes through a message panel.

Changes:

Backend: Replace mock replies with OpenAI chat.completions.create() using mode-specific system prompts; add CORS middleware; fail fast if OPENAI_API_KEY is missing.
Frontend: Add chat panel (message history, input, send button / Enter-to-send), and switch modes in-place while updating cube color.
Add backend Python dependencies file.

In frontend/index.html:

> 
messages.innerHTML += ... reparses and reserializes the entire message history on every send, which can become slow as the list grows. Consider appending DOM nodes (e.g., createElement + textContent) to keep updates incremental and avoid relying on HTML string concatenation.

In frontend/index.html:

> +
+function setMode(mode) {
On non-2xx responses, this assumes the body is JSON (await res.json()). If the backend (or a proxy) returns plain text/HTML for errors, this will throw and you’ll lose the original status/detail. Consider falling back to await res.text() when JSON parsing fails, and include res.status in the surfaced error.

⬇️ Suggested change
-
-function setMode(mode) {
+      let errorBody;
+      try {
+        errorBody = await res.json();
+      } catch (_) {
+        errorBody = await res.text();
+      }
+
+      let message =
+        (errorBody && typeof errorBody === 'object' && errorBody.detail) ||
+        (typeof errorBody === 'string' && errorBody.trim()) ||
+        `Request failed with status ${res.status}`;
+
+      const error = new Error(message);
+      error.status = res.status;
+      throw error;

CORS is configured with allow_origins=["*"] and fully open methods/headers. This enables any website to call this API from a browser, which is risky if the endpoint is publicly reachable. Consider restricting origins (or making them configurable via env) to the expected frontend origin(s).
